segments.arabic: [368] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: حدثنا الليث عن يزيد عن أبي الخير عن عقبة بن عامر قال
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from Yazid, from Abu al-Khayr, from ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir, who said:

segments.arabic: أهدي إلي النبي ﷺ فروج حرير فلبسه فصلى فيه ثم انصرف فنزعه نزعا شديدا كالكاره له، وقال لا ينبغي هذا للمتقين
segments.english: A silk farruj was given to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He put it on and prayed in it. Then, when he finished, he pulled it off forcefully, as though disliking it, and said: “This is not fitting for the God-fearing.”

notes: Farruj remains the source garment term: Fath al-Bari describes a coat split at the back. The unnamed giver remains unnamed. The wearing, prayer, forceful removal, apparent dislike and final statement all remain, without an explanation for the removal imported from another account. Both printed witnesses retain the full report.

segments.arabic: [369] حدثنا محمد بن عرعرة قال: حدثني عمر بن أبي زائدة عن عون بن أبي جحيفة عن أبيه قال:
segments.english: Muhammad ibn ‘Ar‘arah related to us. He said: ‘Umar ibn Abi Za’idah related to me, from ‘Awn ibn Abi Juhayfah, from his father, who said:

segments.arabic: رأيت رسول الله ﷺ في قبة حمراء من آدم ورأيت بلالا أخذ وضوء رسول الله ﷺ ورأيت الناس يبتدرون ذاك الوضوء فمن أصاب منه شيئا تمسح به ومن لم يصب منه شيئا أخذ من بلل يد صاحبه ثم رأيت بلالا أخذ عنزة فركزها وخرج النبي ﷺ في حلة حمراء مشمرا صلى إلى العنزة بالناس ركعتين ورأيت الناس والدواب يمرون من بين يدي العنزة
segments.english: I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in a red leather tent. I saw Bilal take the ablution water of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and I saw the people rushing for that water. Whoever obtained some wiped himself with it, and whoever did not obtain any took some of the moisture from his companion’s hand. Then I saw Bilal take a short spear and plant it. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out in a red outfit, with his garment tucked up, and led the people in two rak‘ahs facing the spear. I saw people and animals passing in front of the spear.

notes: The complete chain is Awn ibn Abi Juhayfah from his father. The Bewley introductory line shortens this differently; it does not replace the selected chain. The two rakahs, absent from that comparison’s body, remain.

Ablution water retains the source’s wording without adding used or left over. The garment being tucked up is retained without adding visible feet or sleeves. The people and animals pass in front of the spear; no wording is added that puts them between the worshipper and the spear. Both printed witnesses retain the full sequence.

segments.arabic: [370] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا سفيان قال: حدثنا أبو حازم قال
segments.english: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: Abu Hazim related to us. He said:

segments.arabic: سألوا سهل بن سعد من أي شيء المنبر، فقال: ما بقي بالناس أعلم مني هو من أثل الغابة عمله فلان مولى فلانة لرسول الله ﷺ وقام عليه رسول الله ﷺ حين عمل ووضع فاستقبل القبلة كبر وقام الناس خلفه فقرأ وركع وركع الناس خلفه ثم رفع رأسه ثم رجع القهقري فسجد على الأرض ثم عاد إلى المنبر ثم ركع ثم رفع رأسه ثم رجع القهقري حتى سجد بالأرض فهذا شأنه
segments.english: They asked Sahl ibn Sa‘d what the pulpit was made of. He said: “There is no one left among the people who knows more about it than I do. It is made of tamarisk from al-Ghabah. So-and-so, the mawla of such-and-such a woman, made it for the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood on it when it had been made and set in place. He faced the qiblah and said ‘Allah is greater,’ and the people stood behind him. He recited and bowed, and the people bowed behind him. Then he raised his head, stepped backwards and prostrated on the ground. Then he returned to the pulpit, bowed and raised his head. Then he stepped backwards until he prostrated on the ground. That was what he did.”

segments.arabic: قال أبو عبد الله قال علي بن عبد الله سألني أحمد بن حنبل رحمه الله عن هذا الحديث قال: فإنما أردت أن النبي ﷺ كان أعلى من الناس فلا بأس أن يكون الإمام أعلى من الناس بهذا الحديث قال: فقلت: إن سفيان بن عيينة كان يسأل عن هذا كثيرا فلم تسمعه منه قال لا
segments.english: Abu ‘Abd Allah said: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah said: Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, asked me about this hadith. He said: “I only meant that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was higher than the people. So, according to this hadith, there is no harm in the imam being higher than the people.” He said: I said: “Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah used to be asked about this often. Did you not hear it from him?” He said: “No.”

notes: The pulpit is of tamarisk from al-Ghabah. The unknown maker and woman remain unnamed. Mawla is retained rather than choosing an unexpressed legal relationship. Stepping backwards is explicit. The historical print and Khan-family comparison include a second recitation; the selected and modern print do not, so none is inserted.

The closing Abu Abd Allah / Ali ibn Abd Allah / Ahmad ibn Hanbal discussion is a visible Transmission note, not Prophetic speech. The source’s mercy honorific and final question to Ahmad about hearing from Sufyan, with his answer No, remain. The matched Khan-family body abridges this discussion; Bewley also omits the compiler attribution and mercy honorific. The selected pronoun He said is not silently replaced with a stronger identification of the speaker. Fath al-Bari discusses the exchange separately.

segments.arabic: [371] حدثنا محمد بن عبد الرحيم قال: حدثنا يزيد بن هارون قال: أخبرنا حميد الطويل عن أنس بن مالك
segments.english: Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahim related to us. He said: Yazid ibn Harun related to us. He said: Humayd al-Tawil informed us, from Anas ibn Malik:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ سقط عن فرسه فجحشت ساقه أو كتفه وآلى من نسائه شهرا فجلس في مشربة له درجتها من جذوع فأتاه أصحابه يعودونه فصلى بهم جالسا وهم قيام فلما سلم قال إنما جعل الإمام ليؤتم به فإذا كبر فكبروا وإذا ركع فاركعوا وإذا سجد فاسجدوا وإن صلى قائما فصلوا قياما ونزل لتسع وعشرين فقالوا يا رسول الله إنك آليت شهرا، فقال إن الشهر تسع وعشرون
segments.english: That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, fell from his horse and his lower leg or shoulder was grazed. He swore to stay away from his wives for a month and stayed in an upper room of his whose steps were made of tree trunks. His companions came to visit him. He led them in prayer while sitting, and they were standing. When he gave the salutation, he said: “The imam is appointed only to be followed. When he says ‘Allah is greater,’ say ‘Allah is greater’; when he bows, bow; when he prostrates, prostrate; and if he prays standing, pray standing.” He came down after twenty-nine days. They said: “Messenger of Allah, you swore for a month.” He said: “The month is twenty-nine days.”

notes: The uncertainty lower leg or shoulder remains. The selected and modern print say tree trunks; the historical print and English comparisons specify date-palm trunks. No tree species is inserted. The upper room, month-long oath, visit, seated imam with standing companions, every instruction and twenty-nine-day reply remain.

This selected report ends its posture instructions with praying standing. The instruction to pray seated that appears in other versions is not imported. No additional legal ruling about the oath or posture is appended.

segments.arabic: [372] حدثنا مسدد عن خالد قال: حدثنا سليمان الشيباني عن عبد الله بن شداد عن ميمونة قالت

segments.arabic: كان رسول الله ﷺ يصلي وأنا حذاءه وأنا حائض وربما أصابني ثوبه إذا سجد قالت وكان يصلي على الخمرة
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray with me beside him while I was menstruating. Sometimes his garment touched me when he prostrated. She said: He used to pray on a khumrah.

segments.arabic: [373] حدثنا عبد الله قال: أخبرنا مالك عن إسحاق بن عبد الله بن أبي طلحة عن أنس بن مالك
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ishaq ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Talhah, from Anas ibn Malik:

segments.arabic: أن جدته مليكة دعت رسول الله ﷺ لطعام صنعته له فأكل منه، ثم قال قوموا فلأصل لكم قال أنس فقمت إلى حصير لنا قد اسود من طول ما لبس فنضحته بماء فقام رسول الله ﷺ وصففت أنا واليتيم وراءه والعجوز من ورائنا فصلى لنا رسول الله ﷺ ركعتين ثم انصرف
segments.english: That his grandmother Mulaykah invited the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to some food she had prepared for him. He ate some of it, then said: “Get up, so that I may pray for you.” Anas said: I went to a mat of ours that had become black from long use and sprinkled it with water. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood, and the orphan and I stood in a row behind him, with the old woman behind us. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led us in two rak‘ahs, then left.

notes: The source’s initial Abd Allah remains unexpanded; the historical print adds ibn Yusuf. The pronoun his grandmother is retained because Fath al-Bari records different identifications of its referent, Anas or Ishaq. No determination is silently inserted. The historical print adds an honorific after Mulaykah which is absent in the selected and modern text; none is added.

The source says our mat and sprinkled it, not my mat and washed it as in the Khan-family comparison. The orphan and old woman remain unnamed, and no ablution or reason for sprinkling is imported from commentary. The complete invitation, meal, arrangement, two rakahs and departure remain.

segments.arabic: [375] حدثنا إسماعيل قال: حدثني مالك عن أبي النضر مولى عمر بن عبيد الله عن أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن عن عائشة زوج النبي ﷺ أنها قالت
segments.english: Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Abu al-Nadr, the mawla of ‘Umar ibn ‘Ubayd Allah, from Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from ‘A’ishah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: كنت أنام بين يدي رسول الله ﷺ ورجلاي في قبلته فإذا سجد غمزني فقبضت رجلي فإذا قام بسطتهما قالت والبيوت يومئذ ليس فيها مصابيح
segments.english: I used to sleep in front of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with my legs in the direction of his qiblah. When he prostrated, he nudged me and I drew my legs in. When he stood, I stretched them out. She said: The houses in those days had no lamps.

segments.arabic: [379] حدثنا آدم بن أبي إياس قال: حدثنا شعبة قال: أخبرنا أبو مسلمة سعيد بن يزيد الأزدي قال:
segments.english: Adam ibn Abi Iyas related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Abu Maslamah Sa‘id ibn Yazid al-Azdi informed us. He said:

segments.arabic: سألت أنس بن مالك أكان النبي ﷺ يصلي في نعليه قال: نعم
segments.english: I asked Anas ibn Malik: “Did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray in his sandals?” He said: “Yes.”

segments.arabic: [380] حدثنا آدم قال: حدثنا شعبة عن الأعمش قال: سمعت إبراهيم يحدث عن همام بن الحرث قال:
segments.english: Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from al-A‘mash, who said: I heard Ibrahim relating from Hammam ibn al-Harith, who said:

segments.arabic: رأيت جرير بن عبد الله بال ثم توضأ ومسح على خفيه ثم قام فصلى فسئل، فقال: رأيت النبي ﷺ صنع مثل هذا
segments.english: I saw Jarir ibn ‘Abd Allah urinate, then perform ablution and wipe over his leather socks. Then he stood and prayed. He was asked about it and said: “I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, do the same as this.”

segments.arabic: قال إبراهيم فكان يعجبهم لأن جريرا كان من آخر من أسلم
segments.english: Ibrahim said: It pleased them because Jarir was among the last to embrace Islam.

notes: Ibrahim’s closing observation is kept as a separate transmission note, with the plural them left unexpanded. segments.arabic: [382] أخبرنا الصلت بن محمد أخبرنا مهدي عن واصل عن أبي وائل عن حذيفة
segments.english: Al-Salt ibn Muhammad informed us; Mahdi informed us, from Wasil, from Abu Wa’il, from Hudhayfah:

segments.arabic: رأى رجلا لا يتم ركوعه ولا سجوده فلما قضى صلاته قال له حذيفة ما صليت
segments.english: He saw a man who did not complete his bowing or prostration. When he finished his prayer, Hudhayfah said to him: “You have not prayed.”

segments.arabic: قال وأحسبه قال لو مت مت على غير سنة محمد ﷺ
segments.english: He said: I think he said: “If you died, you would die following other than the way of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

segments.arabic: [383] أخبرنا يحيى بن بكير حدثنا بكر بن مضر عن جعفر عن ابن هرمز عن عبد الله بن مالك بن بحينة
segments.english: Yahya ibn Bukayr informed us; Bakr ibn Mudar related to us, from Ja‘far, from Ibn Hurmuz, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Malik ibn Buhaynah:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ كان إذا صلى فرج بين يديه حتى يبدو بياض إبطيه،
segments.english: That when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed, he spread his arms apart until the whiteness of his armpits could be seen.

segments.arabic: وقال الليث حدثني جعفر بن ربيعة نحوه
segments.english: And al-Layth said: Ja‘far ibn Rabi‘ah related to me something similar.

notes: The matched Khan-family label is literally 1.8.385u. Its shortened report omits the closing al-Layth / Jafar ibn Rabiah transmission; both Arabic prints and Bewley preserve it. The closing something similar (نحوه) remains, without copying the first body as a repeated quotation.

The historical print uses related to us at Yahya and related to me at Bakr, while the selected and modern text use informed us and related to us respectively. The selected chain and Ibn Hurmuz name remain unchanged. The chapter title concerns spreading the upper arms; no bodily detail beyond the report is added.

segments.arabic: [384] حدثنا عمرو بن عباس قال: حدثنا ابن المهدي قال: حدثنا منصور بن سعد عن ميمون بن سياه عن أنس بن مالك قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
segments.english: ‘Amr ibn ‘Abbas related to us. He said: Ibn al-Mahdi related to us. He said: Mansur ibn Sa‘d related to us, from Maymun ibn Siyah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: من صلى صلاتنا واستقبل قبلتنا وأكل ذبيحتنا فذلك المسلم الذي له ذمة الله وذمة رسوله فلا تخفروا الله في ذمته
segments.english: “Whoever prays our prayer, faces our qiblah and eats what we slaughter is the Muslim who has the protection of Allah and the protection of His Messenger. So do not betray Allah with regard to His protection.”

notes: Dhimmah is provisionally rendered protection, following its covenant/safekeeping sense discussed in Fath al-Bari. The warning against betrayal remains with its source scope. No legal interpretation, additional class of persons or modern application is inserted. Full Amr ibn Abbas / Ibn al-Mahdi / Mansur / Maymun / Anas chain remains.

segments.arabic: [385] حدثنا نعيم قال: حدثنا ابن المبارك عن حميد الطويل عن أنس بن مالك قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
segments.english: Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from Humayd al-Tawil, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: أمرت أن أقاتل الناس حتى يقولوا: لا إله إلا الله فإذا قالوها وصلوا صلاتنا واستقبلوا قبلتنا وذبحوا ذبيحتنا فقد حرمت علينا دماؤهم وأموالهم إلا بحقها وحسابهم على الله
segments.english: “I have been commanded to fight the people until they say: ‘There is no god but Allah.’ When they say it, pray our prayer, face our qiblah and slaughter as we slaughter, their blood and property become forbidden to us except by their due right, and their reckoning is with Allah.”

segments.arabic: قال ابن أبي مريم أخبرنا يحيى حدثنا حميد حدثنا أنس عن النبي ﷺ،
segments.english: Ibn Abi Maryam said: Yahya informed us; Humayd related to us; Anas related to us, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

segments.arabic: وقال علي بن عبد الله حدثنا خالد بن الحرث قال: حدثنا حميد قال
segments.english: And ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah said: Khalid ibn al-Harith related to us. He said: Humayd related to us. He said:

segments.arabic: سأل ميمون بن سياه أنس بن مالك قال: يا أبا حمزة ما يحرم دم العبد وماله، فقال من شهد أن لا إله إلا الله واستقبل قبلتنا وصلى صلاتنا وأكل ذبيحتنا فهو المسلم له ما للمسلم وعليه ما على المسلم
segments.english: Maymun ibn Siyah asked Anas ibn Malik. He said: “Abu Hamzah, what makes a person’s blood and property inviolable?” He said: “Whoever testifies that there is no god but Allah, faces our qiblah, prays our prayer and eats what we slaughter is a Muslim. He has what a Muslim has, and owes what a Muslim owes.”

notes: The selected entry contains a Prophetic statement, an Ibn Abi Maryam / Yahya / Humayd / Anas transmission, and a separate Ali / Khalid / Humayd account of Maymun questioning Anas. All remain in source order. The modern print divides this material across 392 and 393, while the selected source and Bewley retain it under one reference. The matched Khan-family 1.8.387 gives the first and last bodies but omits the middle transmission.

The modern print uses نحروا where the selected and historical print use ذبحوا; the selected Arabic remains unchanged. The wording slaughter as we slaughter in the first statement and eats what we slaughter in the last answer remains distinct. The exception بحقها is rendered by their due right without importing a list of legal grounds. The declaration, complete conditions, property and blood, reckoning, and final rights and obligations all remain. The historical print expands Yahya to Yahya ibn Ayyub and adds an honorific after Allah; neither is inserted into the selected report.

segments.arabic: [386] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا سفيان قال: حدثنا الزهري عن عطاء بن يزيد عن أبي أيوب الأنصارى أن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: Al-Zuhri related to us, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yazid, from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: إذا أتيتم الغائط فلا تستقبلوا القبلة ولا تستدبروها ولكن شرقوا أو غربوا قال أبو أيوب فقدمنا الشام فوجدنا مراحيض بنيت قبل القبلة فننحرف ونستغفر الله تعالى
segments.english: “When you go to relieve yourselves, do not face the qiblah or turn your backs to it, but face east or west.” Abu Ayyub said: We came to al-Sham and found lavatories built facing the qiblah, so we would turn aside and seek the forgiveness of Allah Most High.

segments.arabic: وعن الزهري عن عطاء قال: سمعت أبا أيوب عن النبي ﷺ مثله
segments.english: And from al-Zuhri, from ‘Ata’, who said: I heard Abu Ayyub, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, relate the same.

notes: East then west remains in source order; Bewley reverses that order. The complete closing al-Zuhri / Ata / Abu Ayyub transmission is preserved, though omitted in the matched Khan-family body. The selected Allah Most High remains; the historical print instead has عز وجل.

The source’s al-Sham place name remains. Fath al-Bari discusses the geographic scope of the chapter introduction; that discussion is not inserted as an instruction in the report. The introduction remains separately browsable Arabic with English pending.

segments.arabic: [387] حدثنا الحميدي قال: حدثنا سفيان قال: حدثنا عمرو بن دينار قال
segments.english: Al-Humaydi related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: ‘Amr ibn Dinar related to us. He said:

segments.arabic: سألنا بن عمر عن رجل طاف بالبيت العمرة ولم يطف بين الصفا والمروة أيأتي امرأته، فقال قدم النبي ﷺ فطاف بالبيت سبعا وصلى خلف المقام ركعتين وطاف بين الصفا والمروة وقد كان لكم في رسول الله أسوة حسنة وسألنا جابر بن عبد الله، فقال لا يقربنها حتى يطوف بين الصفا والمروة
segments.english: We asked Ibn ‘Umar about a man who had gone around the House for ‘umrah but had not gone between al-Safa and al-Marwah: could he have intercourse with his wife? He said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came, went around the House seven times, prayed two rak‘ahs behind the Station, and went between al-Safa and al-Marwah. “You have had an excellent example in the Messenger of Allah.” We asked Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, and he said: “He must not approach her until he has gone between al-Safa and al-Marwah.”

notes: The source says We asked in both questions; the Khan-family comparison has I asked at the first one. The selected wording and both printed witnesses preserve the plural. The seven circuits and two rakahs remain, and the final answer belongs to Jabir. The modern print gives the Jabir continuation its own number 396; it remains within selected 387 here.

The report quotes part of Quran 33:21; the chapter heading quotes 2:125. Neither quotation is expanded with surrounding verses. The Station provisionally renders al-maqam; explanatory material is kept outside the report.

segments.arabic: [388] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى عن سيف قال: سمعت مجاهدا قال
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Sayf, who said: I heard Mujahid say:

segments.arabic: أتي بن عمر فقيل له هذا رسول الله ﷺ دخل الكعبة، فقال ابن عمر فأقبلت والنبي ﷺ قد خرج وأجد بلالا قائما بين البابين فسألت بلالا فقلت: أصلى النبي ﷺ في الكعبة قال: نعم ركعتين بين الساريتين اللتين على يساره إذا دخلت ثم خرج فصلى في وجه الكعبة ركعتين
segments.english: Someone came to Ibn ‘Umar and said to him: “Here is the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace; he has entered the Ka‘bah.” Ibn ‘Umar said: I came, but the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had already come out. I found Bilal standing between the two doors. I asked Bilal: “Did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray inside the Ka‘bah?” He said: “Yes, two rak‘ahs between the two pillars on the left as you enter. Then he came out and prayed two rak‘ahs facing the Ka‘bah.”

notes: The selected Sayf remains unexpanded although the modern print adds a name explanation. The full narrator chain, arrival after the Prophet had left, Bilal between the two doors, the two pillars and both sets of two rakahs remain. The selected relative-direction wording is rendered on the left as you enter; no unmentioned architectural reconstruction is added.

This report and the next give different accounts of prayer inside the Kaaba. Both are preserved without reconciling one into the other. Fath al-Bari discusses the distinct accounts and the phrase facing the Kaaba; that discussion remains separate.

segments.arabic: [389] حدثنا إسحاق بن نصر قال: حدثنا عبد الرزاق أخبرنا ابن جريج عن عطاء قال: سمعت ابن عباس قال
segments.english: Ishaq ibn Nasr related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq related to us; Ibn Jurayj informed us, from ‘Ata’, who said: I heard Ibn ‘Abbas say:

segments.arabic: لما دخل النبي ﷺ البيت دعا في نواحيه كلها ولم يصل حتى خرج منه فلما خرج ركع ركعتين في قبل الكعبة، وقال هذه القبلة
segments.english: When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entered the House, he supplicated in all its sides and did not pray until he came out of it. When he came out, he prayed two rak‘ahs in front of the Ka‘bah and said: “This is the qiblah.”

notes: The selected chain ends with Ibn Abbas; Usamah is not added from a different transmission mentioned by commentary. Supplication on all sides, no prayer until leaving, the two rakahs outside and This is the qiblah all remain. Both Arabic printed witnesses retain this account independently of the preceding report.

segments.arabic: [390] حدثنا عبد الله بن رجاء قال: حدثنا إسرائيل عن أبي إسحاق عن البراء بن عازب رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال:
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Raja’ related to us. He said: Isra’il related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

segments.arabic: كان رسول الله ﷺ صلى نحو بيت المقدس ستة عشر أو سبعة عشر شهرا وكان رسول الله ﷺ يحب أن يوجه إلى الكعبة فأنزل الله { قد نرى تقلب وجهك في السماء } فتوجه نحو الكعبة، وقال السفهاء من الناس وهم اليهود { ما ولاهم عن قبلتهم التي كانوا عليها قل لله المشرق والمغرب يهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم } فصلى مع النبي ﷺ رجل ثم خرج بعد ما صلى فمر على قوم من الأنصار في صلاة العصر نحو بيت المقدس، فقال هو يشهد أنه صلى مع رسول الله ﷺ وأنه توجه نحو الكعبة فتحرف القوم حتى توجهوا نحو الكعبة
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had prayed towards Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen or seventeen months. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wished to be directed towards the Ka‘bah. Then Allah revealed: “We have certainly seen the turning of your face towards the sky.” He turned towards the Ka‘bah. The foolish among the people—who were the Jews—said: “What has turned them from the qiblah they had been facing? Say: To Allah belong the east and the west. He guides whom He wills to a straight path.” A man prayed with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then went out after praying. He passed some of the Ansar in the ‘Asr prayer, facing Bayt al-Maqdis. He said that he testified that he had prayed with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and that he had faced towards the Ka‘bah. The people turned until they faced towards the Ka‘bah.

notes: The dual honorific after al-Bara ibn Azib, sixteen-or-seventeen uncertainty and unnamed man remain. The historical print shortens the companion name and omits the honorific; the selected and modern wording remains. The narrator’s who were the Jews phrase is retained as source wording, without any modern generalization.

The selected Quran quotations correspond to portions of 2:144 and 2:142 and remain in their supplied extent. The third-person testimony is retained rather than silently converted to I testify; Fath al-Bari discusses that wording. Bayt al-Maqdis remains the source place name. No companion name, exact date or additional historical explanation is inserted.

segments.arabic: [391] حدثنا مسلم قال: حدثنا هشام قال: حدثنا يحيى بن أبي كثير عن محمد بن عبد الرحمن عن جابر قال:
segments.english: Muslim related to us. He said: Hisham related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir related to us, from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from Jabir, who said:

segments.arabic: كان رسول الله ﷺ يصلي على راحلته حيث توجهت فإذا أراد الفريضة نزل فاستقبل القبلة
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray on his mount wherever it turned. When he intended the obligatory prayer, he dismounted and faced the qiblah.

segments.arabic: [392] حدثنا عثمان قال: حدثنا جرير عن منصور عن إبراهيم عن علقمة قال: قال عبد الله
segments.english: ‘Uthman related to us. He said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from ‘Alqamah, who said: ‘Abd Allah said:

segments.arabic: صلى النبي ﷺ
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed.

segments.arabic: قال: إبراهيم لا أدري زاد أو نقص
segments.english: Ibrahim said: I do not know whether he added or omitted.

segments.arabic: فلما سلم قيل له يا رسول الله أحدث في الصلاة شيء قال وما ذاك قالوا صليت كذا وكذا فثنى رجليه واستقبل القبلة وسجد سجدتين ثم سلم فلما أقبل علينا بوجهه قال إنه لو حدث في الصلاة شيء لنبأتكم به ولكن إنما أنا بشر مثلكم أنسى كما تنسون فإذا نسيت فذكروني وإذا شك أحدكم في صلاته فليتحر الصواب فليتم عليه ثم ليسلم ثم يسجد سجدتين
segments.english: When he gave the salutation, he was asked: “Messenger of Allah, has something new happened in the prayer?” He said: “What is that?” They said: “You prayed such-and-such.” He bent his legs, faced the qiblah and performed two prostrations, then gave the salutation. When he turned his face towards us, he said: “If something new had happened in the prayer, I would have informed you of it. But I am only a human being like you; I forget as you forget. So when I forget, remind me. If any of you is uncertain in his prayer, let him seek what is correct and complete it on that basis, then give the salutation, then perform two prostrations.”

notes: Ibrahim’s uncertainty is a separate transmission note between the opening action and the continuation. It is not attributed to the Prophet, replaced by a known prayer count from a different account, or silently omitted. The full Uthman / Jarir / Mansur / Ibrahim / Alqamah / Abd Allah chain remains; Abd Allah is not expanded to Ibn Masud from the historical print.

The selected dual legs, two prostrations, salutation, turned face, statement about forgetting and final ordered instructions remain. No direction-of-head-turning explanation or extra spoken salutation from the English comparison is inserted.
